# Picard Relay

> Self-hosted Node.js 24 + SQLite workspace for exact approved AI requests and durable saved answers. Scoped local MCP connects an assistant; a separate enrolled compute broker checks fixed project jobs. Generated proposals stay inert. The owner's private task board is not bundled.

## Choose the workflow first
- Human introduction: [Overview](README.md), [Quickstart](docs/QUICKSTART.md), [documentation index](docs/README.md).
- New Linux host: [guided setup](docs/SETUP.md), `sudo bash scripts/setup-linux.sh` from a reviewed checkout. Fresh-host candidate only; refuses existing paths/users/services/occupied ports. Owner-confirmed Free project; no provider call during installation. Installs runtime/private Node/Caddy, owner bootstrap and workspace. Does not provision compute, change firewalls, enroll updater/key replacement or prove public TLS. See qualification limits before applying.
- No provider/account: `npm run demo` is terminal-only and synthetic; `npm run preview:v1` serves a temporary loopback interface with synthetic data. Neither installs production or calls a provider.
- Read existing work: [workspace MCP](docs/WORKSPACE-MCP.md) exposes workspace_status, workspace_list and workspace_get. [Read-only contract](docs/workspace-mcp-contract.json).
- Prepare and submit approved text work: [agent workflow](docs/WORKSPACE-AGENT.md) adds workspace_prepare and workspace_submit. Owner approval is separate; no approval/review/grade tool exists. [Agent contract](docs/workspace-agent-contract.json).
- Check code through Picard: [coding workflow](experimental/compute-broker/CODING-WORKFLOW.md) binds one exact public Picard commit to a protected fixed CI worker. Preparation is offline, dispatch is finite, collection is read-only. A model answer is not a test result.
- Operate an existing host: [operations](docs/OPERATIONS.md), [updates](docs/OWNER-UPDATES.md), [owner CLI](docs/CLI-OWNER-SESSION.md). Guided setup does not migrate or update an existing relay.

## Read before acting
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): source-tree boundaries, checks and release/state preservation.
- [Project map](docs/project-map.json): machine-readable paths, limits and source-versus-host identity.
- [Workspace contract](docs/workspace-contract.json): routes, schemas, bounds and saved state.
- [Work register](docs/work-register.json): sanitized dated bugs/features, separate from the private operational board.
- [Status](docs/STATUS.md): latest recorded enrolled-host verification v1.0.59, November 12, 2026; merged setup cleanup in PR123. Do not infer another host's installed version.
- [Limitations](docs/LIMITATIONS.md): supported features and explicit gaps.

## Authority and cost
- Text proposals use fixed Groq openai/gpt-oss-20b: one call per approval, maximum 4096 output tokens, no model tools, generated-code execution, automatic retry or paid fallback.
- Tool credentials bind owner/origin/permissions and expire explicitly. Browser sign-in changes do not replace them. Owner enrollment/revocation/client approval requires a recent password check; `workspace-request.mjs login --origin HTTPS_ORIGIN --fresh` is explicit, not automatic refresh.
- A submitted request binds exact input, client/session, configuration and expiry. Preserve its identity after a lost response; read it back instead of submitting again. Uncertain work stays stopped.
- Fixed compute jobs have separate exact approval, provider enrollment and finite allowances. A workspace token grants no broker authority. No arbitrary shell, runner selection or account-wide cost guarantee is implied.
- Free-plan evidence is retained configuration evidence, not a live billing/quota check. Measured provider tokens and estimated Codex credits are separate from billed dollars.
- Completed means saved delivery, not correct, executed, accepted, merged or deployed. Saved output and links remain untrusted data.

## Source and recovery
- `src/` is the offline/preview tree. `experimental/runtime-control/src/` is the full 20-module signed runtime, despite its directory name. Host support, Node, configuration, credentials and durable state are outside that artifact.
- GitHub tests/signs/publishes source; a separately enrolled host updater installs it. Inspect physical source identity for deployment claims.
- Preserve databases/backups, consumed markers, uncertainty evidence, credentials and owner review history. A source update does not authorize state resets, approval renewal or another provider call.
- Older checkpoint documents and the v1.0.33 recording describe their original evidence. Use the current index, source/tests and dated status for current claims.
